chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He (the Imam) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servant, but Allah causes the believer to attain from goodness that which He does not cause the disbeliever to attain, so that goodness becomes for him a sign of the greatness of the reward, and it becomes for the disbeliever a sign of the greatness of the punishment.

key_terms.ظَلَّامٍ: Tyrant or one who deals unjustly
key_terms.يَبْلُغُ: To cause to attain or reach

ai.seo_question: How does divine justice explain why believers receive more blessings than disbelievers?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this principle within the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*), emphasizing that worldly prosperity for believers is a test of gratitude and for disbelievers a test of arrogance. This distinction underscores the concept of *Istidraj* (gradual ensnarement) for the latter, where abundance serves as a precursor to intensified punishment, while for the former, it acts as a sign of Allah's favor and increased reward in the Hereafter.
